sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: The aim of this document is to describe the web service Jaggaer One Supplier Management (J1Supplier) in terms of “what is it” and “how to use it”. It describes the webservice data-model, supported operations and related behavior and all available interfaces, including REST and PUSH.
Before going deeper with specific features of this webservice please ensure to review the document “J1P WS Development_Kit - Web Services Overview” which applies to all webservices.
The structure of the current document is the following:
1. Import/Update of Company Data

2. Request data format: describes the possible operations on company (CREATE, UPDATE, CREATE_REGONLY and so on), on classification (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE and so on) and data elements (CREATE). Then, it describes the structure of the request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory depending on the operation you want to perform and those that can be omitted.
3. Behavior: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some particular processes.
4. Response data format: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes.
5. Export of Company Data

6. Component filters [Export of Company Data]: describes which sections of an invoice can be exported. The use of a component filter increments the number of sections in the response to every supplier exported.
Example:

1. Condition filters [Export of Company Data]Condition filters : describes which fields can be used to filter the invoice to be extracted on specific conditions. So, the use of a condition filter allows to decrease the number of suppliers extracted.
2. Result Pagination [Export of Company Data]: describes how the results in response are paginated

3. In order to get the proper subset of results the webservice client can set in the webservice call the parameter startAt (default is 1). Information about the availability of more objects is given by the response parameter nextStartAt. This parameter contains the value to be used for the value of startAt parameter in subsequent request. If there are no available for another request, the response parameter nextStartAt will have the value -1.
In the example above (250 objects, pagination set to 100), the following 3 webservice requests/responses must be executed to have the full list of matching objects
1. Export data format [Export of Company Data]: describes the structure of the response in terms of exported fields and sections.
2. REST INTERFACE
3. Operation and Endpoints: describes REST available collections. Allowed calls with allowed parameters and supported HTTP methods
4. Request samples: contains detailed samples of HTTP request/response for each available operation
5. PUSH INTERFACE
6. Data model: refers to push message data format
7. Configuration: describes configuration options
8. Is Changed: describes the behavior of the “isChanged” attribute
9. Request samples: contains samples of push message

10. Data Types and UI Default Labels: describes the type of the fields and the corresponding label in English language in the platform with the aim to simplify the mapping between the fields visible in the platform and the fields used in the web service.
11. Master Data List: list of available master data

paragraphs: When an update call is done, the web service needs to identify a company to perform the requested operation, even if the update operation is not related to “main” company data but for instance refers to Classification or Data Elements.

sections.title: Supplier Sync process flow when JA is Principal Supplier Management System
paragraphs: As per standard J1 feature supplier are kept aligned between J1 modules. In compliance to these the web-service operates according to the following logic
1. Step 1) the supplier is created or updated in JA using the relevant data-model provided in the webservice call
2. Step2) supplier data are synched between JA and JI, i.e. the supplier is created or updated in JI taking the latest version of JA data
3. Step 3) JI supplier data are enriched with the information provided in the webservice call (JI specific data-model)

sections.title: Supplier Super User when JA is Principal Supplier Management System
paragraphs: The current web-service is aimed at managing supplier company data. Since in JA it is mandatory to have at least one user to create a company, currently the webservice in case of company creation in JA it creates also a “dummy” super-user identified by dummy data.

This user is not synched to JI in the supplier sync internal process flow, then when a supplier company is created no JA users are sent as contacts to JI. Nevertheless, since for several processes, at least one contact is required in JI, it is mandatory for the client component invoking the webservice to specify at least one JI contact.
Supplier Sync process flow when JI is Principal Supplier Management System

When JI is principal there are not automatically supplier sync between systems. The internal supplier sync from JI to JA is a different feature that must be enabled to be used. Therefore, all the fields that are used in the WS under JIData will be passed directly to JI without introducing any business logic.

When an export is executed, both pull and push, JINT will generate the id to be used as J1 ID. This J1 ID is stored in the 3rd Party Ref. Number field JI side then JI is principal. If this is not requested, then it can be deactivated by an internal parameter.

sections.title: Result Pagination [Export of Company Data]
paragraphs: To better manage performances, webservices export responses are limited to a predefined number of items that are configured on a single integration basis (usually it is defaulted to 100 objects per webservice call).

To retrieve the full list of objects matching the provided filtering criteria the webservice client must perform multiple calls, one for each “page”. For instance, if an export call retrieves 250 objects and the maximum is set to 100, the webservice client is required to perform 3 webservice calls, one for objects from 1 to 100, one for object from 101 to 200 and the last for the remaining 50 objects.

In order to get the proper subset of results the webservice client can set in the webservice call the parameter startAt (default is 1). Information about the availability of more objects is given by the response parameter nextStartAt. This parameter contains the value to be used for the value of startAt parameter in subsequent request. If there are no available for another request, the response parameter nextStartAt will have the value -1.
